Rolex – The King of Luxury and Great Investments

﻿

Rolex is the ultimate luxury watch brand. These classic timepieces define the watch industry, and are renowned the world over. Moreover, many models are experiencing eye-popping value appreciation, and have thus become profitable investments.

By René Herold

This page contains information about:

  • Timeless Designs With Investment Potential

Timeless Designs With Investment Potential

Many consider Rolex watches to be the epitome of luxury. Rolex's models are iconic in the watch industry, often serving as the blueprint for entire watch categories. Take for example the Rolex Submariner; although it was by no means the first of its kind, this model is deemed the quintessential diving watch. The GMT-Master was just as influential, radicalizing GMT watches with its two-tone 24-hour bezel.

However, it is not only theexcellent workmanship and stable value that have earned the Geneva-based manufacturer a world-class reputation. Rolex's good name is bolstered by the fact that it has remained independent and attaches great importance to crafting its watches almost entirely in-house. After all, many other well-known watch manufacturers now belong to large corporations; for example, Omega is part of the Swatch Group. Another secret to Rolex's success is their company policy of discretion: tours of their workshops are rare, the CEO seldom gives interviews, and even their annual profits are kept private.

The Five-Point Crown – The History of Rolex

The story of Rolex begins in 1905, when German entrepreneur Hans Wilsdorf, together with Alfred Davis, founded the watch wholesaler Wilsdorf & Davis in London. Davis oversaw the production of the cases, while Wilsdorf sourced the necessary movements from the Swiss company Aegler. In 1908, they trademarked the name “Rolex.” The catchy name most likely comes from "rolling export," but there is no solid proof of the origin.

The five-point crown became a symbol of the brand in 1925. The story behind the development of the logo remains a closely-guarded secret. Experts suspect that the five-pointed crown stands for the five fingers of a watchmaker or the letters in “Rolex.” The crown logo and the name “Rolex” have appeared on every dial, crown, and clasp since 1939.

From the very beginning, Wilsdorf attached great importance to precision. As early as 1910, he had his timepieces tested. To this day, every Rolex is certified as a "Superlative Chronometer" and deviates from the standard time by a maximum of -2/+2 seconds per day.

Shortly after his wife's death, he left all of his Rolex shares to the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation. The Foundation is owned by Rolex and receives a large portion of its annual profits. This money is used to support social initiatives, environmental programs, and scientific, artistic, and cultural projects.

How much does a Rolex cost?

As of spring 2026, official list prices for current Rolex watches range from 6,940 USD to 199,338 USD. Most of the Geneva-based manufacturer's watches are difficult to obtain from authorized dealers, and waiting times can be considerable. If you don't want to end up on a long waiting list, the only option is the secondary market. However, given limited supply and high demand, you should expect significant price premiums.

This is reflected in the price of the stainless steel Submariner Date ref. 126610LN, which costs 15,378.98 USD on Chrono24 – that’s several thousand more than the official list price. You’ll have to dig even deeper into your pockets if you want to own a Daytona ref. 126500LN with a white dial or the stainless steel GMT-Master II ref. 126710BLRO. At 36,258.71 USD and 23,724.58 USD respectively, these models are priced at around twice the MSRP. Prices for the latter in particular are expected to rise further, as Rolex discontinued all "Pepsi" models in April 2026 without replacing them.

Things aren’t always that pricey; vintage models from the 1930s and 40s can be found on Chrono24 from around 1,166 USD.

What’s the most affordable Rolex?

The most affordable Rolex watches on Chrono24 are vintage models from the 1940s and 50s, which you can buy from around 1,166 USD. However, these are purely collector's items with no prospect of significant appreciation. Stable vintage models such as the Rolex Precision ref. 4498 or the Rolex Cellini ref. 4112 range in price from approx. 4,082 USD to 5,832 USD. If you are looking for an affordable unisex watch from the current Rolex range, the Oyster Perpetual 36 (ref. 126000) is your best choice. Depending on the dial color, you should budget between approx. 9,331 USD and 17,496 USD for an unworn watch.

What’s the most expensive Rolex?

The most expensive Rolex watch ever sold is the Cosmograph Daytona owned by Hollywood legend Paul Newman. In 2017, Phillips auction house sold the ref. 6239 with a tricolor exotic dial for a staggering record sum of $17.75 million.

The auction ensured a sustained run on exotic dial Daytona models, now known as the Rolex “Paul Newman.” Particularly popular models include the references 6239, 6241, and 6264 with the aforementioned dial variation. Prices for these stainless steel watches range from 233,280 USD to over 449,064 USD. The gold variants of these references – also known as the "John Player Special" – usually break the million mark with ease.

But make no mistake, even newer Daytona models have been raking in six-figure sums. You should plan to spend at least 509,474.17 USD for a Rainbow Daytona 116595RBOW.

Men's Watches From Rolex

Rolex offers a huge selection of men's watches. Sports models such as the Submariner, Yacht-Master, or Sea-Dweller are particularly suitable for larger wrists with diameters of 37 to 43 mm. The Rolex Deepsea Challenge comes in at an impressive 50 mm.

Men will also find plenty to choose from in the Rolex dress watch collections. In addition to unisex sizes, the manufacturer also offers special men's models that are between 39 and 41 mm.

When it comes to dials, men tend to opt for the traditional black Rolex. Blue Rolexes are also popular. Rolex Meteorite, i.e., watches with dials made of meteorite rock, are truly one of a kind.

Rolex Ladies' Watches

Many Rolex watches can be worn by both men and women. In addition to unisex models, the manufacturer also offers some watches that are specifically aimed at women. Rolex watches with mother-of-pearl dials and diamonds look particularly feminine and elegant. One example is the Rolex Lady-Datejust. It offers the same design features as the standard Datejust models, but with a diameter of 28 mm, it is better suited to slimmer wrists. You can find older versions on Chrono24 that are slightly smaller at 26 mm.

The Oyster Perpetual 26 is a more affordable alternative. It is likewise 26 mm, but does not have a date display.

Datejust: The Classic Dress Watch

The Datejust has been a cornerstone of Rolex’s catalog since 1945. Since the release of the 40th Anniversary Edition, this timepiece has defined what it means to be a sporty dress watch. Its simple design, with a narrow bezel, slender baton hands, and a Cyclops lens date display at 3 o'clock, has remained virtually untouched since the very first model, the ref. 4467. The Jubilee bracelet, which debuted alongside the Datejust, also remains in the Rolex catalog to this day.

The original version of the Rolex Datejust has a diameter of 36 mm. Rolex has since expanded the range to include other sizes. You can find variants on Chrono24 measuring 26, 28, 31, 34, 36, and 41 mm across. As for materials, you have the choice between stainless steel, white gold, yellow gold, rose gold, and two-tone combinations of gold and stainless steel. There are also a wide range of dial designs to choose from.

Features of the Rolex Datejust

  • Sporty dress watch with cult status
  • Date display with Cyclops lens
  • Men's and women's models
  • Large selection of dial designs
  • Available in stainless steel, gold, and two-tone versions
  • Jubilee bracelet

Rolex Submariner: A Pioneer Among Diving Watches

The Submariner is undoubtedly one of the classics in the Rolex lineup and hailed as the archetypal modern diver.

The current versions of the Submariner are water-resistant to 300 m (30 bar, 984 ft) and are available in stainless steel, white gold, yellow gold, or two-tone gold and steel. You can also choose between a Submariner without a date display and the Submariner Date.

The collection offers a wide range of model variants. These include the "Hulk,""Kermit," and "Submariner COMEX."

Features of the Current Rolex Submariner

  • 41 mm in diameter
  • Available in stainless steel, gold, and two-tone versions
  • Models with or without a date
  • Water-resistant to 300 m (30 bar, 984 ft)

Rolex Daytona: An Icon Among Chronographs

The Cosmograph Daytona is one of Rolex's most popular watches. First introduced in 1963, the chronograph is named after the legendary Daytona Beach racetrack in Florida. As is typical of Rolex, the design of the watch has remained more or less unchanged to this day. Characteristic features include the tachymeter bezel, tricompax dial layout, and screw-down push-pieces.

Vintage versions from the 1960s and 70s are coveted by collectors. Particularly well-preserved "Paul Newman" models with a so-called "exotic dial" garner top prices at auction.

Features of the Rolex Daytona

  • Tricompax design
  • Fixed bezel with a tachymeter scale
  • Screw-down crown and push-pieces
  • Water-resistant to 100 m (10 bar, 328 ft)
  • Available in stainless steel, gold, platinum, or two-tone variants

Day-Date: The Presidential Watch

In 1956, Rolex made history once again with the release of the Oyster Perpetual Day-Date, a.k.a. the Rolex President. It was the first wristwatch capable of displaying both the date and day of the week written out in full. Like the Datejust, its date display is located under a Cyclops lens at 3 o'clock, while its additional day window arcs over the famous Rolex crown at 12 o'clock. Rolex also created a unique bracelet for the Day-Date: the President Bracelet.

The watch is exclusively available in gold or platinum. It is available in sizes of 36 and 40 mm. Similar to the Datejust, Rolex also offers the Day-Date with countless dial variants. Overall, however, the Day-Date has a more dignified appearance, which makes it ideal for formal occasions.

Features of the Rolex Day-Date

  • Date display, and day of the week written out in full
  • Cyclops lens
  • Available in 36 or 40 mm
  • Gold or platinum case
  • President bracelet

Rolex GMT-Master and GMT-Master II

Rolex originally developed the GMT-Master for Pan Am pilots. The GMT-Master and its successor, the Rolex GMT-Master II, more or less set the standard for watches with a second time zone.

At first glance, the GMT-Master strongly resembles the Submariner. However, if you take a closer look, you'll see several differentiating factors. The most obvious difference is the 24-hour bezel. On most models, this bezel is usually divided into two colors to distinguish between day and night. The most popular color combinations are red and blue (Rolex Pepsi), black and red (Rolex Coke), blue and black (Rolex Batman), brown and black (Rolex Root Beer), green and black (Rolex Sprite), and black and gray.

Another difference is the additional central GMT hand, which, together with the bezel, indicates the time in a second time zone. This makes the GMT-Master an ideal travel watch for keeping track of both local and home times.

In spring 2026, Rolex surprised the watch world with its decision to discontinue all Rolex GMT-Master II watches with the iconic red and blue "Pepsi" bezel without replacement. Many industry experts assume that the Geneva-based manufacturer will present a successor in the near future. However, it remains to be seen if and when this will happen.

Features of the Rolex GMT-Master

  • GMT watch (second time zone)
  • Colorful 24-hour bezels
  • Water-resistant to 100 m (10 bar, 328 ft)
  • Available in stainless steel, gold, or two-tone editions

Vintage Watches From Rolex

Most of Rolex's model series can look back on a history of more than 50 years. The range of vintage Rolex watches is correspondingly large. Collectors are mainly looking for early versions of classics such as the Submariner, GMT-Master, or Daytona. Watches with naturally aged tropical dials, where the color has changed due to sunlight and humidity, are also sought-after collector's items.

You will also find numerous simple Rolex watches from the 1940s and 50s on Chrono24, which are suitable for beginners due to their relatively low prices.

New Rolex Releases From Watches and Wonders 2026

The Rolex innovations at Watches and Wonders 2026 centered around the 100th anniversary of the Rolex Oyster. Accordingly, the Oyster Perpetual has many new features. Models with a diameter of 28 and 34 mm are now available in yellow or rose gold versions. Rolex offers the Oyster Perpetual in 31, 36, and 41 mm sizes as a "100 Years" special edition. These watches are two-tone stainless steel and yellow gold. The manufacturer also replaced the usual "Swiss Made" lettering below the 6 o'clock position with the words "100 Years." The winding crown likewise features "100." Friends of colorful dials will delight in variants of the Oyster Perpetual with the Jubilee dial. The motif, in which the word Rolex is repeated, has been used by the manufacturer since the 1970s. This time, the design got a colorful makeover.

New Colors and Materials for the Day-Date, Datejust, and Daytona

There are new color and material variants for the Day-Date, Datejust, and Daytona. The Day-Date is now available in the brand-new Jubilee Gold alloy, which ranges in color between yellow, rose, and gray gold. A Rolesor version of the Datejust 41 with a green lacquered ombré dial is also now available. The Daytona collection is enriched by a model that comes with an all-white enamel dial, a retro-style Cerachrom bezel, and a case made of Rolesium (stainless steel and platinum).

The Yacht-Master II Refurbish

While the previously mentioned innovations were more cosmetic in nature, Rolex completely redesigned the Yacht-Master II. The newly developed caliber 4162 now powers the watch. It still provides the Yacht-Master II with a programmable countdown timer. However, this is now operated via the pushers on the watch – making the ring command bezel of older models a thing of the past.

Overview of 2026 Rolex Releases

FAQ

Which Rolex watch is worth investing in?

Rolex watches are generally characterized by excellent value stability. Almost all Rolex watches are therefore suitable as an investment. Rare vintage models generally offer the best chance of increasing in value.

Will the prices of Rolex watches continue to rise?

Rolex has increased its list prices on average every 12 months in recent years. This is unlikely to change in the future. However, prices on the secondary market have fallen noticeably since 2022. Nevertheless, they are still significantly higher than the list prices.

Why is Rolex so expensive?

Rolex watches are highly coveted. They are characterized by exquisite quality, high precision, innovative technology, and unique designs. As status symbols with a high level of prestige, they also offer excellent potential for value appreciation, which further increases their appeal.

It's very difficult to buy a Rolex from offline retailers. At the same time, demand is extremely high, which in turn drives prices upward. Rolex is renowned for their premium quality, high precision, and innovative designs. As a result, Rolex watches enjoy tremendous prestige and are often considered status symbols. What's more, Rolex models are highly likely to increase in value, which also contributes to the brand's appeal.
The Rolex Daytona Ref. 6263 fetched 17.8 million USD at auction in 2017, and is therefore the most expensive Rolex of all time. This model is also known as the Paul Newman Daytona, as it was the Hollywood actor and race car driver's watch of choice. The Daytona was given to him by his wife Joanne Woodward in 1969. The case back is engraved with the loving message, "Drive Carefully Me."
Prices for Rolex watches start at around 2,000 USD. This amount will get you a pre-owned model in stainless steel. Premium models like the Daytona Rainbow can cost over 1 million USD. The Submariner Date is one of Rolex's most popular watches. The current reference 126610 costs around 15,500 USD new on Chrono24.
